newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 17.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Tuesday:
* Buoyed by the popularity of large utility and four-wheel-drive vehicles, American car makers are about to push out even larger models that come with large sticker prices.
* A dispute has broken out on Capitol Hill as to whether states or the federal government should decide how to spend the $16 billion earmarked for health care for uninsured children.

* The debate over rent-control laws went down to the wire, leaving New York's tenants nervous and frazzled. But that's just the way things are done at the state Capitol, where deals are brokered at the last minute.
* The Irish Republican Army shot dead two Northern Ireland policemen, prompting the British Government to call off contacts with the IRA's political arm, Sinn Fein.
* Federal prosecutors in Manhattan are seeking the death penalty in a case gainst a man accused of nine murders as part of his role as head of a drug gang.
* The European Union moved ahead with plans for a single currency, turning aside French concerns that the alliance's top priority should be unemployment, not budget deficits.
